svg.title: Why testing poses close enough together proves the whole move
svg.text: Proving a whole move from tested poses (option A of Q3, schematic)
One straight machine move (X, Y, Z and A linear) from a kept point to the next. Tested poses at every halving level.
a sharp edge between two tested poses: only the bound catches it
D: the most any point of the tool moves between them
Every point of the tool at a pose between two tested poses is within D/2 of the same point at one of them
(halfway is the worst case). So no surface point can be deeper inside it than the deeper of the two readings plus D/2.
Rule: keep the move when every tested pose clears to within (tolerance less D/2); otherwise test more poses or halve it.
A ball moving without turning gains less than D/2 (the sagitta, D squared over 8R), so it needs fewer poses; a flat end's corner gains up to D/2.
D counts both the tip's travel and A's turn times the furthest distance of the cutting part from the rotary axis.
